skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Browser automation through inference.sh for opening pages, using element refs, interacting with forms, capturing screenshots or video, routing through proxies, and running page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Automates browser sessions with element refs, screenshots, video, proxy support, and extraction workflows.
skill.author: inf-sh

security_audit.summary: The skill is a powerful browser automation wrapper with legitimate documentation and templates, but it exposes high-risk dual-use capabilities. Confirmed risks include a curl-to-shell installer, browser screenshots and videos, SOCKS proxy routing, arbitrary page JavaScript, cookie extraction guidance, and proxy rotation for rate-limit avoidance. Most shell, URL, path traversal, and /dev/null static matches are documentation examples or benign shell plumbing.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh in the quick start.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell install command with package-manager instructions, checksums, or a reviewed script download step.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes cookie extraction from authenticated sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie extraction examples or limit them to explicit debugging guidance with strong warnings and no credential material output.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation includes rate limit avoidance and anonymity-oriented workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove rate-limit avoidance language, require permission-based use, and frame proxies for corporate testing or regional QA only.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and recordings can capture sensitive authenticated page content.
remediation.suggestion: Default examples should disable recording for login flows and clearly warn users before capturing private pages.

remediation.issue: The execute function allows arbitrary JavaScript in page context.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe extraction boundaries and warn against running untrusted JavaScript or extracting secrets from authenticated pages.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Sessions with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser workflows slow research, testing, and data collection. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code drive pages through inference.sh with element refs, screenshots, video, and scripts.
actual_capabilities: Open URLs and return the page title, current URL, elements, and screenshots.
Use @e element refs to click, fill, select, drag, upload, scroll, and navigate.
Refresh page snapshots after navigation, form submission, or dynamic content changes.
Capture viewport screenshots, full-page screenshots, and optional session video.
Route browser sessions through HTTP, HTTPS, or SOCKS proxy settings.
Run JavaScript in the current page context for extraction and verification.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated inference.sh account.
Browser traffic, screenshots, and videos are handled by an external service.
Element refs expire after navigation or major page changes.
Templates need review before use with credentials or private sites.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Flows
use_cases.description: Run browser steps, inspect element refs, and capture screenshots for repeatable web checks.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Open public pages, extract visible text and links, and save screenshots for analysis.

use_cases.title: Document Support Workflows
use_cases.description: Record guided browser sessions that show each interaction and final page state.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to open <url> in a new session. Show the title, current URL, and available element refs.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open <form_url>, identify the refs for each field, fill the provided values, submit the form, and snapshot the result.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence for a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Open <url> with video enabled, perform these steps: <steps>. Capture a final screenshot and close the session.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Authenticated Proxy Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Open <url> through <proxy_url>, log in using environment variables, avoid recording sensitive fields, capture the final state, and close the session.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and identify the add-to-cart control.
output_examples.output: A concise page summary with the current URL, visible title, key element refs, and the ref for the add-to-cart button.

output_examples.input: Record a settings workflow for documentation.
output_examples.output: A completed session with step results, a final screenshot reference, and a video file reference returned after close.

output_examples.input: Extract visible text and links from a public page.
output_examples.output: A short extraction summary with page title, main text sections, discovered links, and any interaction notes.

best_practices: Take a fresh snapshot after navigation, form submission, or dynamic content changes.
Use environment variables or a secrets manager for credentials and proxy passwords.
Close sessions promptly and store screenshots or videos only when they are needed.
anti_patterns: Do not automate sites without permission or ignore terms, rate limits, or access controls.
Do not pipe remote installers directly to a shell without review and verification.
Do not use stale refs or unreviewed templates for destructive account actions.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser sessions through inference.sh, including navigation, element interaction, screenshots, video, proxies, and page JavaScript.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on the inference.sh CLI and sends browser automation requests to that service.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated sites?
faq.answer: Yes, but credentials and session content must be handled carefully and recordings should be disabled for sensitive flows.

faq.question: How do element refs work?
faq.answer: The browser returns short @e refs for visible interactive elements, and later actions use those refs.

faq.question: When should I refresh a snapshot?
faq.answer: Refresh after navigation, form submission, modal changes, or other DOM updates because refs can expire.

faq.question: Is proxy support included?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation shows HTTP, HTTPS, authenticated, and SOCKS proxy settings for browser sessions.
